headline: Add customer KYC onboarding, compliance verification, and account-opening gate
summary: Introduces the Customers module with customer registration, age validation, and compliance officer verify/reject workflows backed by a new Customers table. Registers KycAccountOpeningRule so account opening requires a verified customer record, and exposes customer and compliance HTTP endpoints.
business: New applicants aged 18 or older must register and wait for a compliance officer other than themselves to verify their identity before opening a bank account. Unverified or underage applicants are blocked from opening accounts.

reasons.text: Class-level Customer policy prevents compliance officers from verifying or rejecting registrations
reasons.claim: In ASP.NET Core, Authorize attributes combine cumulatively across controller and action levels. Because [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] is declared on the CustomersController class, Verify and Reject require callers to satisfy both Customer and Compliance policies simultaneously, blocking compliance officers who do not hold customer credentials.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the CustomersController class declaration so that each action's method-level [Authorize] attribute controls access independently.
reasons.say: Compliance officers cannot verify or reject customer registrations unless they also hold a customer account. Ask the author to remove the class-level policy from CustomersController so staff can review applications.
reasons.say_facts: Because [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] is declared on the CustomersController class, Verify and Reject require callers to satisfy both Customer and Compliance policies simultaneously, blocking compliance officers who do not hold customer credentials. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.text: Class-level Authorize attribute inadvertently requires Customer policy on Compliance endpoints
reasons.claim: In ASP.NET Core, class-level and action-level [Authorize] attributes are combined with logical AND. Specifying [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] on CustomersController forces callers of Verify and Reject to satisfy both Policies.Customer and Policies.Compliance, causing HTTP 403 Forbidden for compliance officers who do not possess the Customer role.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from line 14 on CustomersController so that endpoints rely strictly on their individual method-level [Authorize] attributes.
reasons.say: Compliance staff will be blocked with access denied errors when trying to approve or reject applicants. Check CustomersController and ensure compliance endpoints do not also require customer permissions.
reasons.say_facts: Specifying [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] on CustomersController forces callers of Verify and Reject to satisfy both Policies.Customer and Policies.Compliance, causing HTTP 403 Forbidden for compliance officers who do not possess the Customer role. Ask for a fix before merging.

reasons.detail: New applicants aged 18 or older must register and wait for a compliance officer other than themselves to verify their identity before opening a bank account. Unverified or underage applicants are blocked from opening accounts.
reasons.say: Underage or unverified applicants are blocked from opening bank accounts, and staff cannot verify their own applications. Verify that these onboarding safeguards and conflict-of-interest rules match bank policy.
reasons.say_facts: This change has a high impact on customers or money: New applicants aged 18 or older must register and wait for a compliance officer other than themselves to verify their identity before opening a bank account. Unverified or underage applicants are blocked from opening accounts. Confirm the business owner agrees.

reasons.text: Redundant and conflicting controller-level Authorize attribute
reasons.claim: Applying [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level causes ASP.NET Core to evaluate it conjunctively for every action in the controller. This makes lines 27 and 46 redundant and inadvertently forces Verify and Reject (lines 56 and 79) to require both Customer and Compliance policies, risking authorization failures for compliance officers.
reasons.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the CustomersController class declaration so that each action exclusively enforces its own explicit Authorize policy.
reasons.say: The controller-level customer access rule makes individual customer endpoint rules redundant and blocks compliance staff from reviewing applications. Ask the author to restrict the customer policy to customer endpoints only.
reasons.say_facts: This makes lines 27 and 46 redundant and inadvertently forces Verify and Reject (lines 56 and 79) to require both Customer and Compliance policies, risking authorization failures for compliance officers. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: CustomersController endpoints lack unit or integration tests
reasons.claim: The newly introduced CustomersController and its four endpoints (Register, Me, Verify, Reject) have no unit or integration tests. Routing, HTTP status code mapping (200, 400, 403, 404, 409), and policy authorization attributes ([Authorize(Policy = ...)]) are entirely unexercised by the test suite.
reasons.suggested_fix: Add controller tests verifying endpoint execution, status code translation for exceptions (BadRequest, Forbid, NotFound, Conflict), and authorization policy metadata.
reasons.say: None of the four new customer and compliance endpoints have automated tests for access rules or responses. Ask the author to add tests proving unauthorized users are blocked and errors return properly.
reasons.say_facts: Routing, HTTP status code mapping (200, 400, 403, 404, 409), and policy authorization attributes ([Authorize(Policy = ...)]) are entirely unexercised by the test suite. Decide whether it must be fixed now.

reasons.text: 11 changed method(s) have no usable test evidence
reasons.say: Eleven new or changed methods, including the registration, profile, and verification endpoints, lack test evidence. Ask for test coverage proving customer onboarding and staff verification work reliably before approving.
reasons.say_facts: 11 changed parts of the code are not covered by any working test. Read them yourself or ask for tests.
